samples.summary: `POST .../slides` seeds placeholder blocks from an unbanded master, writing out-of-band typography into the CRDT — bypassing the master band this change adds
samples.evidence:
`apply()` calls `op(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot()))`, and `readSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52) applies no band at all. `slide-ops.addSlide` hands that document to `new MemSlidesStore(document)`, whose `addSlide` seeds `blocks: seedPlaceholderBlocks(placeholderStyle, theme)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:210) and then the controller `splice`s the resulting slide onto the live `root.slides`.

The frontend equivalent bands at exactly this point and says why: yorkie-slides-store.ts:1318-1324 — "this is the reader that actually feeds `seedPlaceholderBlocks`: without it a poisoned master's `fontSize` is *committed* to the CRDT inside the blocks a layout change seeds, where a later read band would only hide it from this client." The backend copy of that path has no `bandMasterNumerics` call.

Attack: a collaborator (or an earlier `PUT` made before this branch) writes `masters[0].placeholderStyles.body.fontSize = 1e9` via `doc.update`. Any workspace member then calls `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/slides` with a `title-body` layout. The seeded blocks are persisted with `fontSize: 1e9`, which is now stored content rather than a per-reader artefact. The new write-side band in `assertValidSlidesBody` (`bandMasterPlaceholderStyles`) does not run on this route, and the read-side band only hides the value from clients that happen to re-band.
searchedFor: Grep bandMasterNumerics across repo (no backend hits)

samples.summary: The new MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS / normalizeColumnRatio band is bypassable through a slides `table` element's `data.columnWidths`, which is capped on neither write nor read
samples.evidence:
`bandSlideBlockNumerics` (docs-content.controller.ts:1120-1128) newly caps a docs *block* table's `columnWidths` to `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (256) and maps every entry through `normalizeColumnRatio`, and `parseColumnWidthsAttr` does the same on the CRDT read side. The sibling shape — a slides *element* of `type: 'table'` — gets neither.

Write side: `assertValidTableData` (line 946) only checks `columnWidths` is an array; no length cap, no per-entry band. Read side: `bandElementNumerics` for `el.type === 'table'` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-83) walks only `data.rows[].cells[].body.blocks` and never touches `data.columnWidths` or `rows[].height`.

Sink: `computeTableLayout` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:86-99) sets `nCols = columnWidths.length` and runs `for r in nRows { for c in nCols }`, and `colX[c+1] = colX[c] + columnWidths[c]`. So a `PUT /content` body carrying a `table` element with ~2M `columnWidths` entries (≈12 MB, inside the 25 MB `JSON_BODY_LIMIT`) and 1000 rows produces ~2e9 iterations per layout pass for *every* viewer of the deck, and a single `Infinity`/`-1e400` entry produces NaN cumulative offsets that blank the table. This is the same amplification and the same NaN-geometry outcome the change explicitly bands for the docs-block twin, reached through the path the band skipped.

samples.summary: `bandMasterNumerics` indexes a plain object literal with an untrusted key, so a prototype-chain key defeats the band for that placeholder slot
samples.evidence:
`for (const key of Object.keys(styles))` iterates attacker-supplied keys from `placeholderStyles`, then `DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles[key] ?? DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles.body` is a bare property read on an object literal typed `{ [key: string]: PlaceholderStyle }` (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:29-36).

For `key === 'constructor'` the read resolves to `Object` (a function, so truthy — the `??` fallback never fires); for `'toString'`/`'valueOf'` it resolves to a function; for `'__proto__'` it resolves to `Object.prototype`. In every case `fallback.fontSize` and `fallback.lineHeight` are `undefined`, so the band writes `style.fontSize = undefined` / `style.lineHeight = undefined` into a field the type declares as a required number. The slot is then unbanded in the sense that matters: `seedPlaceholderBlocks` copies `undefined` into a docs `Block`, and the empty-placeholder hint builds a `NaNpx`/`undefinedpx` canvas font.

The controller under review avoids exactly this pattern deliberately one file over — `EMPTY_ELEMENT_DATA` is a `Map` "so the untrusted `type` string can never reach a prototype key" (docs-content.controller.ts:910-918). The same reasoning applies here and was not carried across. Note this is not prototype *pollution*: the write targets the own entry object, not the prototype.
searchedFor: Read EMPTY_ELEMENT_DATA Map rationale in docs-content.controller.ts:907-924

samples.summary: An attacker-controlled, unbounded-length object key is reflected verbatim into the 400 response body
samples.evidence:
`bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` builds `const slotPath = `${path}.placeholderStyles.${slot}`` from `Object.entries(styles)` and interpolates it into `new BadRequestException(`Invalid master at ${slotPath}: '${field}' must be a number`)` (line 624-626). `slot` is a raw JSON object key from the request body, subject only to the 25 MB `JSON_BODY_LIMIT`.

Every other error message in this file interpolates only internal enums or numeric indices (`blocks[3]`, `slides[0].elements[2]`), so this is the first untrusted free-form string echoed back. Concretely: a `PUT` whose `masters[0].placeholderStyles` has one key of ~10 MB and a `fontSize: "x"` yields a ~10 MB error body reflected to the caller, and the same content is what NestJS logs. Low direct impact for a JSON API (no HTML context), but it is unvalidated input on the response path and an easy response-amplification primitive; truncating or omitting `slot` would remove it.
searchedFor: Reviewed all other BadRequestException template strings in docs-content.controller.ts

samples.summary: The new recursion depth cap covers only elements and blocks; `themes`, `guides`, slide `background`, and the `data` of unrecognised element types still reach Yorkie with unbounded nesting
samples.evidence:
`MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` is justified (line 791-805) by "the walk recurses ... and the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint." That threat statement is about the *writer*, not only the validator, but the cap is applied to exactly three walks.

Uncapped paths on the same `PUT`: `assertValidSlidesBody` checks `themes`/`guides` are arrays and never descends; `assertValidSlide` checks `background` is an object and never descends; `assertValidElementData` falls through with no walk for any `type` outside text/shape/table/chart/group (e.g. `type: 'image'`). All of those are then handed to `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93-110), which assigns them straight onto the Yorkie root proxy — a recursive CRDT build over the nesting depth. A `{type:'image', data:{a:{a:{…}}}}` chain, or a deeply nested `themes[0]`, therefore reaches the writer at whatever depth survived body parsing.

I could not confirm reachability end to end, which is why confidence is low: V8's `JSON.parse` inside `bodyParser.json` may itself throw `RangeError` on extreme depth, returning a 400 before the handler runs — in which case this gap (and arguably the new cap itself) is unreachable over HTTP. The new tests build 20 000-deep structures programmatically rather than through `JSON.parse`, so they do not settle it either way. If the cap is load-bearing, these sibling fields need it too; if `JSON.parse` already rejects, that is worth recording so the cap is not mistaken for the thing holding the line.
searchedFor: Read assertValidSlidesBody / assertValidSlide / assertValidElementData in docs-content.controller.ts

samples.summary: The docs `PUT` persists an entirely unvalidated `styles` blob to `root.stylesJson`; the new guarantee rests solely on every reader remembering to call `sanitizeDocStyles`
samples.evidence:
`writeDocsRoot` does `root.stylesJson = JSON.stringify(document.styles)` (line 349-350) for whatever `styles` the request body carried, and `assertValidDocsBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:304-325) validates `blocks`, `header` and `footer` and never inspects `styles` — the change's own comment concedes this ("the v1 `PUT` validator never inspects it", crdt-tree.ts:322).

This change closes the hole on the read side only, in two places: `docsTreeToDocument` (crdt-tree.ts:329) and `YorkieDocStore.getStyles` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:830). I verified those are currently the only `JSON.parse(stylesJson)` sites, so no live bypass exists today. The structural weakness is that the registry reaches `resolveStyleInline`/`resolveStyleBlock` — described in `sanitizeDocStyles`'s own JSDoc as "one string that bypasses `normalizeFontSize` and `normalizeLineHeight` everywhere at once" — and nothing at the write boundary stops the poisoned value being *stored*. Any future reader that parses `root.stylesJson` directly (a server-side export, a migration, a new preview adapter) silently inherits the full hole, and `sanitizeDocStyles` deliberately passes unknown keys and unknown sub-properties through untouched, so the stored blob is also an unbounded attacker-controlled payload served to every peer. Banding on write as well would make this fail closed.
searchedFor: Grep stylesJson across the repo (all read sites enumerated)

verdict.reason: The claimed path exists exactly as described and is unguarded. slides.controller.ts:174 calls op(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())); slides-tree.ts:64-67 returns root.masters verbatim with no bandMasterNumerics. slide-ops.ts:162-170 hands that unbanded deck to MemSlidesStore, whose addSlide (memory.ts:181-211) reads this.doc.masters directly (not through read()/migrateDocument, neither of which bands) and seeds blocks via seedPlaceholderBlocks, which copies style.fontSize/lineHeight verbatim (placeholder-blocks.ts:30,38). The controller then splices that slide onto the live CRDT root.slides (slides.controller.ts:186-191), persisting out-of-band typography as stored content. The write-side band is confined to the other route: docs-content.controller.ts:196 -> assertValidSlidesBody -> bandMasterPlaceholderStyles (:588); grep shows zero band* usage anywhere in packages/backend/src outside that file, so no guard makes this path unreachable. The repo's own frontend comment (yorkie-slides-store.ts:1318-1324) states precisely why banding must happen at this seeding reader rather than only on read. Reachable by any ordinary collaborator/write-scoped API key passing CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard, so it is unsafe handling of peer-writable untrusted input that the repo elsewhere treats as a security control. No refutation ground available.

The sink is unguarded: computeTableLayout (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:86-92, 96-133) sets nCols = columnWidths.length, accumulates colX[c+1] = colX[c] + columnWidths[c] (non-finite entry poisons all later offsets), and runs two nRows x nCols loops; drawTable only early-returns on nCols === 0. verdict.reason: The absence is real and I verified it myself. assertValidSlidesBody (docs-content.controller.ts:560-566) only type-checks `themes` as an array and never descends into it; `guides` is not validated at all (repo grep for `guides` in the file yields nothing outside a doc comment); assertValidSlide (:718) accepts `background` on `typeof === 'object'` with no walk; assertValidElementData (:835-905) increments `depth` only for `group` children and returns without any walk for element types outside text/shape/table/chart/group (e.g. `type:'image'`). All four reach writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:97-109), which assigns them directly onto the Yorkie root proxy inside doc.update (controller :244-252). I searched wide for a counterexample guard rather than re-reading the reviewer's spots: repo-wide grep for depth/MAX_DEPTH/nest across packages/**/*.ts, main.ts (only JSON_BODY_LIMIT and a global ValidationPipe that cannot constrain an untyped `@Body() body: unknown`), yorkie.service.ts#withDocument (:71-116, no sanitisation), and yorkie-json.ts (read path only, itself unbounded recursion). The only other depth caps in the tree are document-image-refs.ts:156 and slides band-numerics.ts:39, neither on this route. The reviewer's reachability doubt does not save it: V8's JSON parser has been iterative since V8 7.6, so bodyParser.json will parse a deeply nested 25 MB body and hand it to the handler, making the new cap load-bearing and these sibling fields a hole in it. Residual uncertainty is impact only (a stack RangeError in a sync handler is catchable -> 500, and the route is behind CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard/ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard), which is why confidence is low rather than the existence of the gap being in doubt.

searchedFor: read packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts in full, checking every recursive helper's signature for a depth parameter
grep for MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH / depth in the controller

finding.summary: The slides PUT validator's nested-block walk recurses without a depth cap (`assertValidSlideBlocks` → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` → `assertValidSlideBlocks` through `tableData.rows[].cells[]`), while the sibling element walk in the same file caps at 32 citing exactly this stack-exhaustion risk on this authenticated endpoint.
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks(blocks, path)` (line 1084) takes no `depth` parameter; at line 1135 it calls `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, cellPath)` which calls back into `assertValidSlideBlocks` (line 998) for the cell's own `blocks`, unbounded. The same file justifies `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at line 729-735 with 'the walk recurses through `data.children` and the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint' — the identical argument applies here, and to `assertValidBlock` (line 437, recursing into `cell.blocks` at line 478). One nested-table level costs ~50 bytes, so ~50k levels (≈2.5 MB, far under the body limit) is a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` thrown from inside `PUT /content`. The newly added `bandSlideBlockNumerics`/`bandSlideCellNumerics` calls sit on this same unbounded walk, so the hardening inherits the gap instead of closing it.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing depth cap is present. `assertValidSlideBlocks` is declared as `(blocks, path, depth = 0)` and immediately throws `BadRequestException('...blocks are nested too deeply')` when `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (docs-content.controller.ts:1160-1169). The table-cell recursion increments it: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, cellPath, depth + 1)` at :1220, and `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (:1055-1070) and `assertValidTextBody` (:1021-1030) both thread `depth` back into `assertValidSlideBlocks`, so the counter is monotonic across the mutual recursion. The docs-arm walk the finding also cites as uncapped, `assertValidBlock`, likewise caps at :438-447 and recurses with `depth + 1` at :488-492. The MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH doc comment at :791-806 explicitly states the ceiling is shared by both block walks for precisely the stack-exhaustion reason the finding raises. All entry points (:315, :742, :862) start at the default depth 0, and the element/block counters are independent, bounding total frames. Regression tests pin the behaviour (docs-content.validation.spec.ts:82-102, asserting /nested too deeply/ for nested slide text bodies, slide notes, and docs bodies). The finding's cited line numbers (1084, 1135, 998, 437/478) do not match the current file, indicating a stale revision was reviewed.
